messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — High: autoscaler queue growth detected against gpu-pool-az3. Queue length trending up, > 300 pending requests, throttling observed.

jordan (oncall): saw the alert, I'm looking. Which tenant is the highest impact?

lina (support): multiple customers reporting 5xx and long tail latency. CS ticket REF-3321 for outbound API errors. One enterprise customer reported timeouts for heavy-batch embedding jobs.

samir (infra): checking scheduler logs and MIG utilisation. Initial grep: 
```
Scheduler: fail to place pod: no matching node: fragmented free slices (requested 8g.16g nodes available as 1x8g + 1x4g)
Placement: binpack score dropped 0.2
```

maya (runtime): autoscaler tried to scale up but hit pool limit for this region (quota cap 24 GPUs). Requests got queued then throttled by request-router.

jordan (oncall): summary: fragmentation + scale ceiling => stranded capacity + queue growth. Immediate mitigation options?

samir (infra): incremental actions: 1) temporarily relax MIG size constraints to allow smaller-slice packing, 2) trigger emergency capacity bump to the burst pool (if available), 3) move low-priority jobs to the preemptible lane. Which can we do fastest?

maya (runtime): relaxing MIG profiles needs cluster reboot of a subset of nodes -> ~5-7m rolling. We can also patch scheduler to allow mixed-MIG placement (fast, <2m) but risk on-CPU blowups.

jordan (oncall): go with mixed-MIG placement patch first, then hit burst pool. Patch + roll should be safe. samir, can you produce the patch?

samir (infra): on it. Pushing patch to allow 4g+2x2g packing for requests that accept smaller KV cache. Command I ran: 
```
git checkout -b relax/mix-mig
kubectl apply -f scheduler/placement-mix.yaml
```
Patch applied to scheduler-canary nodes. Monitoring logs.

ops-bot: deploy started by samir. canary targets: scheduler-canary-{2,3}. Rollout id 7c9f.

maya (runtime): canary accepted mixed slices, we placed 28 pending pods in canary nodes with no OOMs. Queue dropped 40% in 90s.

lina (support): CS update: REF-3321: we saw reduced errors but enterprise still reporting occasional 504s. Publishing interim note to affected customers.

jordan (oncall): good. Now second mitigation: request burst pool allocation. samir can you open a capacity request with cloud admin? If no burst capacity, we'll reroute large batch embeddings to dedicated-standby.

samir (infra): opened CR 7542 with cloud-admin. They confirmed nominal burst pool available in us-west but needs manual approval. I've requested immediate approval and started failover plan.

maya (runtime): failover plan: update routing rule to send requests with header `x-priority: low` to preemptible-pool; header `x-tenant: enterprise` keep on main route. Will take ~3-4m to flip.

jordan (oncall): do the preemptible flip now for non-enterprise. lina, coordinate CS message to ask customers to mark jobs as low-priority to avoid timeouts.

lina (support): sending note now.

ops-bot: routing-change initiated by maya: route-rule-id=rc-9912.

maya (runtime): routing change applied. Observed queue length drop to 45 pending within 2m. Latency 95th improved from 12s -> 3.2s for low-priority traffic. Enterprise bucket still at 6-8s 95th.

jordan (oncall): we still have stranded slices due to asymmetric MIG sizing on older nodes. Next steps: plan a rolling compact (drain nodes with tiny slices and re-provision with uniform MIG configs). That requires maintenance window or canary first.

samir (infra): I can start a targeted drain for 3 low-util nodes to defragment binpacking. Command: 
```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-old-12
kubectl drain node/gpu-old-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
Doing one at a time to avoid mass migration.

maya (runtime): be careful — draining will temporarily increase scheduler pressure. Let's keep autoscaler patched and routing set while drains proceed.

jordan (oncall): agree. Start drain sequence, monitor for queue spikes. If queue > 200 again, revert routing.

samir (infra): drain started on gpu-old-12. Evicted 18 pods; 14 successfully rescheduled to mixed-MIG nodes. 4 pending due to affinity — manually rescheduling.

incident-bot: NOTE: on-call handoff scheduled in 30m. jordan handing to next-oncall (samir) at 1959876580.

jordan (oncall): I'm going to handoff to samir in 5m. Samir you own the follow-up runbook: ensure drains finish, confirm cloud-admin approval for burst pool, and coordinate full defrag plan.

samir (infra): taking handoff. I'll keep updates in this thread.

lina (support): CS message posted: customers advised of partial degradation; workaround: set jobs to low-priority to avoid retries.

maya (runtime): final notes before handoff: revert flags if any stability regressions seen; keep mixed-MIG enabled for next 2 hours while drains complete. Also create regression alert for 95th latency crossing 10s.

samir (infra): cloud-admin approved burst pool. We requested +6 GPUs for 30m window. Allocated, now adding to capacity groups. Queue fell under 20 now.

jordan (oncall): thanks everyone. handing to samir now. I'm available if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

samir (infra): confirmed — taking over. Follow-ups tracked: 1) full node re-provisioning plan (ETA 48h), 2) adjust autoscaler quota thresholds to avoid silent cap hits, 3) post-incident RCA to include MIG sizing policy and scheduling heuristics.

ops-bot: incident resolved? severity downgraded to medium — queue stabilized and major customer impact mitigated.

lina (support): closing CS interim alerts; will follow up with impacted customers once RCA ready.

samir (infra): closing thread for now; will file RCA ticket (INC-7542-RCA) and link eval traces.
